neighbours.label: a near miss in events: ' almost' or ' nearly' before what did not quite happen, and 'as if it had been' (almost fell, almost quit, nearly killing), as opposed to the same event happening and ' almost' as a quantity
fire: He tripped on the step and I almost fell too.
She was so tired that she almost gave up.
The car skidded, nearly hitting a child.
It felt almost as though it happened in a dream.
I remember it as if it had been last week.
We very nearly missed the last train.
He almost drowned in the river as a boy.
I almost forgot to call you.
quiet: He tripped on the step and I fell too.
She was so tired that she gave up.
The car skidded and hit a child.
It felt strange and it happened in a dream.
I remember it and it was last week.
We just missed the last train.
Almost all of the boys swam in the river.
Nearly half of the class is here.

notes: 'Almost all' reached 0.15 in a probe; ' almost' and ' nearly' for quantity are in the near misses.
